Goal: re-establish movement patterns, breathing, pelvic floor activation, joint mobility, and confidence.

Brief overview
- Diastasis recti (DRAM) = separation of the linea alba causing a gap between the two rectus abdominis muscles. Screening at home can give a useful indication but is not a formal diagnosis; a pelvic-health physio can provide an objective assessment (finger-width measure, inter-recti distance, tension of linea alba, and functional testing).
- Because she hasn’t been checked formally, screen now and periodically as you progress to detect increased separation, doming/bulging, or loss of tension during exercises. If you find concerning signs, pause or regress loading and refer to a pelvic-health physiotherapist.

When to screen
- Baseline now (10 weeks postpartum) before increasing intensity.
- Re-check every 2–4 weeks or whenever you see symptoms (bulging, new urinary leakage, pelvic heaviness, pain) or before moving to higher-impact or heavy-loading progressions.

How to perform a practical, safe at-home screening (step-by-step)
1) Preparation and coaching cues
- Have the client lie on her back with knees bent (hook-lying), feet flat on the floor, hips and knees about hip-width apart.
- Coach breathing first: 2–3 diaphragmatic breaths (inhale to ribs/abdomen, exhale fully), then a gentle pelvic-floor "lift and draw in" cue. Emphasize no breath-holding or forceful bearing down.
- Explain what to look/listen for: gap size (finger widths), tissue softness/tension (is the linea alba firm or mushy), and whether any bulging or doming occurs when she lifts her head/shoulders slightly.

2) The basic curl/head-lift test (self or clinician-assisted)
- From hook-lying, ask her to gently lift her head and shoulders a small amount as if doing the start of a crunch — just enough to feel abdominal engagement (about 1–2 inches). Alternatively, for an even gentler test, ask for a posterior pelvic tilt or pelvic curl (tilt pelvis toward ribs) while maintaining neutral breathing.
- While she does this, you (trainer) or she with a mirror/palpation can feel along the midline from just above the pubic bone to just below the xiphoid process with the fingers (index and middle fingers together or three fingers stacked — see below).
- Palpate perpendicular to the linea alba (across the midline) and find the widest point of separation. Note three things:
  a) Width (number of finger-widths that fit into the gap).
  b) Location (approx pubic, umbilical, supraumbilical).
  c) Tension/quality of the connective tissue when she lifts: is there a firm, slightly springy tension (good) or a soft/mushy/absent tension and visible doming/bulging (concerning)?

3) Interpreting finger-widths (general guidance, not diagnostic)
- 0–1 finger width: generally considered within normal range.
- 2 fingers: borderline; monitor and use symptom guidance.
- 3+ fingers: larger separation — be cautious with loading and refer for formal physio assessment.
Note: finger-width is imprecise and influenced by finger size; use it as a screening tool, not definitive diagnosis.

4) Observe for doming/bulging and functional signs
- During the head lift or gentle sit-to-stand, watch the midline for doming or coning (a ridge or bulge). If present, reduce abdominal compression work and refer.
- Ask about symptoms: urinary leakage during coughing/lifting, pelvic heaviness, or pain with activities — these suggest pelvic floor involvement and need assessment.

5) Functional load checks (progression screening)
- While performing breath-coordinated exercises (dead bug, pallof press, farmer carry, plank on knees), watch for:
  - Visible doming/coning along the linea alba.
  - Increased bulging with exhalation or strain.
  - New or increased urinary leakage or pelvic heaviness.
- If any occur, regress the exercise (reduce range, revert to earlier regressions, shorten holds, reduce load) and schedule a physio referral.

How to document findings (simple tracking)
- Record date, test used (head-lift/hunch or pelvic tilt), widest finger-count, level (sub-umbilical/umbilical/supraumbilical), tissue quality (firm/soft), presence of doming (yes/no), and any symptoms (leakage/pain/heaviness).
- Repeat and compare every 2–4 weeks; look for reduced gap, improved tension, or any worsening.

Progression rules based on screening results
- If gap ≤ 1–2 fingers and no doming or symptoms: progress through the on-ramp as planned, continuing anti-flexion/core and pelvic-floor work.
- If gap ~2 fingers with good tension and no symptoms: proceed cautiously—prioritize anti-flexion work, breath coordination, and gradual load increases.
- If gap ≥ 3 fingers OR any bulging/doming OR symptoms (leakage/heaviness/pain): stop advanced loading/progression, revert to low-load core (diaphragmatic breathing, pelvic-floor activation, gentle dead bugs, heel slides), reduce carries/plank time, and refer to pelvic-health physiotherapist for assessment and guided rehab before resuming progression.

Coaching cues during the test to improve accuracy and safety
- Cue gentle exhale as she lifts head/does small movement; avoid Valsalva.
- Encourage a soft pelvic-floor contraction (not a squeeze so hard it holds breath) as she tests.
- If palpating, be gentle — line above the pubic bone can be tender.

When to refer
- Any of the following: gap ≥3 finger-widths, soft/mushy connective tissue with poor tension, visible doming/coning during small movements, new or worsening urinary incontinence, pelvic organ prolapse symptoms (heaviness/pressure), or pelvic pain.
- Also refer if you’re unsure about your findings — better to get a formal pelvic-health physiotherapy screen.

Below is the consolidated 4-week on-ramp (weeks 1–4) for your 10-week postpartum client, with all adjustments rolled in: anti-flexion core, pelvic-floor micro-sessions, low-impact cardio, one weekly HIIT (seated bike) beginning mid-week 2/Week 3, progressive intensity after she felt good mid-week 2, screening guidance for diastasis/pelvic-floor checks, and safe regressions. Assumptions: home setting, light dumbbells (e.g., 2–8 kg), resistance band optional, mat, stable chair/step, stationary bike available. Continue to avoid jumping and standing bike sprints until formally cleared. Monitor symptoms continuously (doming/coning, urinary leakage, pelvic heaviness, pain). If any appear, stop progression and refer to pelvic-health physiotherapist.

Overview
- Frequency: 3 strength sessions/week (Mon/Wed/Fri suggested), daily 3–5 min pelvic-floor/core micro-session, 2–3 low-impact cardio sessions/week plus 1 HIIT session/week introduced in Week 3, 1–2 active recovery walks as tolerated.
- Warm-up for every session: 5–8 minutes (diaphragmatic breathing, pelvic-floor cueing, joint mobility, light cardio).
- Cool-down: 4–6 minutes mobility and breathing.
- Screening: perform a diastasis/pelvic-floor quick screen at baseline (now), before increasing intensity (mid-week 2), end Week 3, and end Week 4 — or anytime symptoms occur.

Daily micro-session (every day, 3–5 minutes)
- Diaphragmatic breathing with pelvic-floor cue: 6 slow breaths.
- Pelvic-floor quicks: 10 quick lifts.
- Pelvic-floor holds: 5 holds x 6–8 sec with normal breathing.
- Dead-bug or supine heel slides: 1–2 sets x 6–10 reps each side (gentle).

Progression & safety principles
- Increase one variable at a time (weight, sets, reps, complexity, tempo, or cardio intensity).
- Keep breathing coordinated: exhale on exertion; avoid Valsalva.
- Check midline during heavier sets for doming/coning. Stop and regress if present.
- Screening thresholds: ≤1 finger width generally fine; 2 fingers borderline — proceed carefully; ≥3 fingers or soft linea alba or doming/any pelvic symptoms → regress and refer.

Week 1 — Acclimatisation (lower volume, technique focus)
Goal: re-establish pelvic-floor breathing, anti-flexion core patterns, movement quality, and confidence.

Structure: Strength Mon/Wed/Fri + 2 low-impact cardio sessions (short) + daily micro-session.

Warm-up (each session, 6–8 min)
- Diaphragmatic breathing 1–2 min, pelvic-floor cueing.
- Joint mobility: cat-cow, hip circles, shoulder rolls.
- March or easy pedal 2–3 min.

Week 1 — Session A (Mon) — ~30–35 min
- Glute bridge — 2 x 10–12 (pause 1 sec at top; cue pelvic-floor engage).
- Incline/wall push-up — 2 x 8–10.
- Supported one-arm DB row (hand on chair) — 2 x 10 each side.
- Bodyweight squat to chair — 2 x 10–12 (slow eccentrics).
- Dead bug (bent-knee) — 2 x 8 each side, exhale on reach.
- Farmer hold (light DBs) — 2 x 30 sec.
- Core add: Pallof press (band or DB front hold) — 2 x 20–25 sec each side.
- Cool-down breathing and gentle hamstring/hip flexor stretches.

Week 1 — Session B (Wed) — ~30 min
- RDL with light DBs — 2 x 10–12 (hip hinge focus).
- Seated or supported overhead press — 2 x 8–10 each side.
- Step-ups to low step — 2 x 8 each leg.
- Side-lying clamshells — 2 x 12–15 each side.
- Bird-dog (hands/knees) — 2 x 8 each side (2–3 sec hold).
- Core add: Side plank on knees — 2 x 12–20 sec each side.
- Cool-down.

Week 1 — Session C (Fri) — ~30–35 min
- Glute bridge march — 2 x 8–10 each side.
- Reverse lunges (assisted) — 2 x 8 each leg.
- Two-arm bent-over row with DBs — 2 x 10–12.
- Pallof press or anti-rotation hold — 2 x 20–25 sec each side.
- Standing calf raises — 2 x 12–15.
- Cool-down.

Cardio Week 1
- Brisk walk 20–25 min on two non-consecutive days OR one short seated bike easy 15–20 min + one walk 20 min.
- Keep intensity low–moderate; monitor symptoms.

Screening (baseline)
- Perform diastasis/head-lift check now (hook-lying small head lift or pelvic tilt) — document finger-width, location, tissue tension, and any doming. If gap ≥3 fingers or doming, regress program and refer.

Week 2 — Build foundational capacity (increase sets/volume slightly)
Goal: increase strength capacity and core anti-flexion endurance; keep intensity cautious. Mid-week 2 screening before pushing further.

Warm-up similar each session.

Week 2 — Session A (Mon) — ~35–40 min
- Glute bridge — 3 x 12 (progress to single-leg 2 x 6–8 if form perfect).
- Incline push-up — 3 x 8–10.
- One-arm row support — 3 x 10 each side.
- Goblet squat with light DB — 3 x 10–12.
- Dead bug progression — 3 x 8–10 each side.
- Farmer carry — 3 x 30–45 sec.
- Core add: Pallof press — 3 x 25–30 sec each side.

Week 2 — Session B (Wed)
- RDL with DBs — 3 x 10–12.
- Standing DB overhead press — 3 x 8–10.
- Reverse lunge — 3 x 8–10 each leg.
- Lateral band walk or side steps — 3 x 10 each way.
- Bird-dog with 3–4 sec hold — 3 x 8 each side.
- Core add: Modified plank on knees — 2 x 20–25 sec.

Week 2 — Session C (Fri)
- Hip thrust or glute bridge (progressed) — 3 x 10–12.
- Static split squat — 3 x 8 each side.
- Two-arm bent-over row — 3 x 10–12.
- Pallof press half-kneeling or standing — 3 x 25–30 sec each side.
- Single-leg balance/mini-squats — 2 x 8–10 each side.
- Cool-down.

Cardio Week 2
- 2 low–moderate sessions (20–25 min): one seated bike steady or intervals (e.g., 5 x 2 min moderate / 2 min easy seated) and one brisk walk 25 min.
- Mid-week 2: perform diastasis/pelvic-floor quick screen before increasing intensity. If everything stable (no doming, no leakage, gap small or improving), apply the mid-week push adjustments below. If symptoms present, maintain Week 2 volume and consult physio.

Mid-week 2 push adjustments (only if screening good and client feels great)
- Increase load slightly on compound lifts (add ~2–3 kg) OR add 1 set to main lifts (e.g., from 3 to 4 sets) — do one change only per lift.
- Increase farmer carry durations by ~15–30 sec.
- Increase seated bike steady ride from 20 to 25 min or add one more interval (e.g., 5 → 6 x 2/2).

Week 3 — Add intensity and HIIT introduction (conservative)
Goal: increase load, unilateral work, and introduce 1 weekly seated-bike HIIT. Continue daily core micro-sessions and ongoing screening.

Warm-up each session. Keep breathing/pelvic-floor cues before heavy work.

Week 3 — Session A (Mon) — ~40 min
- Single-leg RDL (bodyweight or light DB) — 3 x 8 each side.
- Knee or incline push-ups — 3 x 8–12.
- Bent-over single-arm row — 3 x 10 each side.
- Goblet squat — 3 x 10 (add slight tempo control on eccentric).
- Dead bug with longer lever — 3 x 10 each side.
- Farmer carry heavier — 3 x 45–60 sec walks.
- Core add: Pallof press 3 x 30–35 sec each.

Week 3 — Session B (Wed) — ~40 min
- RDL with slightly heavier DBs — 3 x 8–10.
- Standing DB overhead press — 3 x 8–10.
- Reverse lunge to balance — 3 x 8–10 each leg.
- Side-lying clamshells with band — 3 x 15.
- Bird-dog to side-plank progression (knees) — 2 x 20–30 sec each side.
- Core add: Modified plank on knees 3 x 20–30 sec.

Week 3 — Session C (Fri) — ~40 min
- Hip thrust (heavier if tolerated) — 3 x 8–10.
- Split squat with DB — 3 x 8 each side.
- Two-arm bent-over row heavier — 3 x 8–10.
- Pallof press longer holds — 3 x 35–40 sec each.
- Single-leg calf raises — 3 x 10–12 each side.
- Core circuit finisher (optional): Dead bug 10 each, bird-dog 8 each, plank knees 20–30 sec — 2 rounds.
- Cool-down.

Cardio Week 3 (includes first HIIT)
- HIIT (Seated bike) — 1 session/week (start this week). Choose Option 1 or 2 based on tolerance:
  - Option 1 (safe intro): Warm-up 6–8 min seated easy; 8 x (20 sec hard / 40 sec easy) all seated; cool-down 5–8 min.
  - Keep RPE ~7–8 short bursts; remain seated; avoid breath-holding.
- Plus 1 steady ride or brisk walk 25–30 min on another day.
- Place HIIT session on a separate day from the heaviest lower-body strength day if possible or allow 48+ hours recovery.

Screening Week 3
- Diastasis/pelvic-floor re-check end of Week 3. If stable, you may continue increased intensity. If any doming, leakage, or increased gap, stop HIIT and regress to steady-state cardio and lower-load strength; refer to pelvic-health physio.

Week 4 — Consolidation and higher but cautious intensity
Goal: consolidate gains and prepare to transition to more regular programming. Increase intensity modestly, longer carries, longer anti-flexion holds, possibly a second HIIT only if absolutely symptom-free (recommended: keep HIIT to 1/wk).

Week 4 — Session A (Mon) — ~40–45 min
- Single-leg RDL or heavier RDL — 3 x 8–10.
- Push-ups progress (knees/full if safe) — 3 x 8–12.
- One-arm row heavier — 3 x 8–10 each.
- Goblet squat with tempo (2 sec down) — 3 x 10.
- Plank progression: plank knees or try 1 set toes if no doming — 3 x 20–40 sec total.
- Farmer carry — 3 x 60 sec.
- Core add: Pallof 3 x 40–45 sec each.

Week 4 — Session B (Wed)
- RDL heavier — 3 x 8.
- Standing overhead press — 3 x 8–10.
- Walking lunges controlled — 3 x 10 steps each leg.
- Lateral band walks — 3 x 12 each way.
- Tall-kneeling band roll-out (short range) or modified anti-extension — 2 x 6–8 (only if core control very good).
- Core add: Side plank 3 x 30 sec each side (knees or full as tolerated).

Week 4 — Session C (Fri)
- Hip thrust heavier — 3 x 8–10.
- Bulgarian split squat — 3 x 8 each side.
- Bent-over row — 3 x 8–10.
- Single-leg calf raises — 3 x 12 each.
- Anti-flexion core circuit: Dead bug 10 each, Pallof 30–40 sec each, Plank 30 sec — 2–3 rounds as tolerated.
- Cool-down and breathing.

Cardio Week 4
- Maintain 1 HIIT session/week (option to keep to 1 only) — progress either to 10 rounds or slightly longer intervals (e.g., 6 x 1 min hard/1.5–2 min easy) if symptom-free.
- Two steady sessions: one 30–35 min ride or brisk walk and one 25–30 min easy recovery ride/walk.
- Avoid hills/standing sprints.

Screening Week 4
- Final program re-check: diastasis/pelvic-floor screening at end of Week 4. If stable, and no symptoms for several weeks, you can begin run trials per the conservative running reintroduction plan (start only if cleared and typically earliest ~12–16+ weeks postpartum).

HIIT and fat-loss considerations
- HIIT limited to 1/week to start; increase to 2/week only after 2–4 weeks symptom-free and good recovery. Keep 48+ hours between HIIT and heavy lower-body lifts.
- Nutrition: moderate calorie approach—avoid aggressive deficits postpartum. Protein target ~1.2–1.6 g/kg bodyweight (adjust for breastfeeding). Pre-HIIT snack 30–60 min prior (small carb+protein). Post-workout protein + carb within 1–2 hours.
- Hydration & sleep are priority for recovery and milk supply if breastfeeding.

Screening quick checklist before each heavier session / HIIT
- Any urinary leakage with recent activity? Y/N
- Any pelvic heaviness/pressure today or after prior workouts? Y/N
- Any visible doming/coning on brief test? Y/N
- Diastasis finger-width (if checking): ___ fingers; tissue quality (firm/soft): ___
- If any Yes or gap ≥3 fingers/soft tissue → regress and refer.

Regression ladder (if symptoms appear)
- Reduce load (drop DB weight).
- Reduce lever/complexity (dead bug long lever -> bent-knee dead bug; plank toes -> knees).
- Reduce duration/volume (halve carry time/holds, drop sets).
- Replace HIIT with steady-state bike/walk until symptoms resolve.
- Refer to pelvic-health physiotherapist for formal assessment and tailored rehab.

Coaching cues (general)
- Exhale on exertion; keep a gentle pelvic-floor lift on the exhale; do not hold breath.
- Keep ribs soft and neutral spine — avoid excessive arching.
- Look for any midline ridge during effort — if present, stop and regress.
- Prioritize quality reps and breathing over heavier load.
